Practical 1

System Maintenance and Planning

Reading a system log to find what went wrong, and planning the routine checks that catch faults before they become outages.

Reading a Log

One line per event, oldest at the top. Neither failure below begins at the red lines - both begin with something small near the top.

Also in sample_system_log.txt and sample_backup_log.txt in this folder, if you would rather scroll them in an editor.

Log 1 - the server, over three days

Loading the log...

Log 2 - the backups, over two weeks

Loading the log...

Three questions, in groups

Answer all three for each log - Give each group ten minutes, then one person reports back. The disagreements are the useful part.

  1. What is going on? What changed through the day, when did it start going wrong, and what finally broke?
  2. How would you resolve it? What would you do first, in what order, and who would you tell while you work?
  3. What would stop it happening again? Turn your answer into one line for your plan in Activity 2. 
# Packages used: none. These are built into the terminal.

# A log is plain text, so ordinary text tools are enough to search it.

# Show the last 20 lines - what happened most recently
tail -20 sample_system_log.txt

# Pull out only the errors, ignoring the routine chatter
grep ERROR sample_system_log.txt

# Every line that mentions disk space, to watch one number over three days
grep "Disk space" sample_system_log.txt

# The same trick on the backup log: every failed off-site copy, in order
grep "off-site" sample_backup_log.txt

# How many warnings in each? A rising count is itself a warning.
grep -c WARNING sample_system_log.txt
grep -c WARNING sample_backup_log.txt
